4f4881f26f3cfa39: BANGKA: The Bangka slow loris is one of Earth's most exotic primates, a slow-moving tree dweller that happens to be venomous.
It was listed as critically endangered and possibly extinct, last scientifically documented in the 1930s, but now has been rediscovered on the tropical Indonesian island of Bangka.
Scientists revealed in a new study that an animal rescue organisation came across more than 90 Bangka slow loris individuals in recent years on Bangka, located off the southeastern coast of Sumatra.
Most were returned to the wild.

"The Bangka slow loris is still alive," said Timon Glaw, a graduate student in nature conservation and biodiversity management at the Haus des Meeres Aqua Terra Zoo in Vienna, Austria, and one of the authors of the study published in the journal Spixiana.
The rescued animals came from different parts of Bangka, showing the species has survived in several areas despite extensive habitat destruction and decades of scientific neglect, Glaw said.
Its habitat has been diminished due to tin mining and land clearing for oil palm plantations, Glaw said.
"What I find particularly astonishing is that such a charismatic and distinctive primate has received so little scientific attention for nearly a century.
"Its rediscovery also offers hope that other species feared to be extinct may still survive in places where scientists have not looked for decades.
"After all, Bangka is just about an hour flight from Jakarta, one of the largest cities in the world," Glaw said.
The Bangka slow loris, whose scientific name is Nycticebus bancanus, is a relatively small, nocturnal primate, with reddish-brown fur, distinctive facial markings and large eyes.
It moves slowly and deliberately in the trees, unlike other arboreal primates such as apes, monkeys and lemurs that can move quickly across branches.
In the primate evolutionary lineage, the Bangka slow loris is more closely related to the lemurs of Madagascar and the galagos of Africa than to monkeys or apes — or people.
"The last historical scientific records from Bangka discussed in our study date back to the early 1930s, more precisely to the period between 1930 and 1932.
"For decades, there was no reliable information on whether the species survived on the island," Glaw said.
In 2020, the International Union for Conservation of Nature, the organisation that monitors the status of species, deemed the Bangka slow loris critically endangered and possibly extinct.
The species also was listed as one of the "lost primates" by the conservation group Re:wild.
Like the world's other slow loris species, it is venomous — a rare trait among mammals.

Slow lorises produce a secretion from specialised glands near their elbows, which they mix with saliva by raising their arms when threatened and then licking the glands before delivering the venom through a bite.
"The venom can cause severe allergic reactions in humans, potentially even life-threatening ones.

"Research on other slow loris species suggests that the venom is used primarily in conflicts with other lorises, although it may also serve defensive functions against predators and parasites," Glaw said.
Its diet is not well understood, but it likely feeds on insects, tree gums, nectar and other plant parts like other slow loris species, Glaw said.

It possesses a toothcomb formed by forward-projecting lower teeth, used mainly for grooming, gouging of tree bark for gum and delivering the venom during bites. It also has a specialised second tongue beneath the main tongue that helps clean the toothcomb.
Between 2015 and 2025, the Indonesian conservation organisation Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center documented more than 90 Bangka slow lorises from different localities across the island, Glaw said.
Many were rescued from houses, gardens, plantations or roads, while others suffered severe injuries, particularly from electrical wires, with a few dying despite treatment, Glaw said.
Following their recovery, 86 of them were released into suitable natural habitats, Glaw said.
"The most urgent priority is to protect the remaining natural forests on Bangka from further destruction, particularly through tin mining and the expansion of oil palm plantations.
"We also need systematic field surveys to determine where the species still survives and how large its populations are," Glaw said.
"Every species is the result of millions of years of evolution and part of a complex ecological network, and losing the Bangka slow loris would mean losing something truly irreplaceable," Glaw said.

59167264db3e5abf: KUALA LUMPUR: A Barisan Nasional MP today urged all parties to exercise consistency when debating the discretionary powers given to an attorney-general to discontinue criminal proceedings, following the conditional discharge granted to deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi in his Yayasan Akalbudi case.

Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah) said there were many cases in which an attorney-general discontinued criminal proceedings and the accused was acquitted, including those of former Pandan MP Rafizi Ramli, former Batu Berendam MP Tamrin Abdul Ghafar and Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Karim.
Adnan also cited the discontinued prosecution of Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan) and businesswoman Phang Li Koon in a corruption case involving the purchase of a bungalow.
"If prosecutorial discretion was accepted in previous cases, why can’t similar principles be applied to the case involving Bagan Datuk (Zahid)?
"This is not about defending any individual or political party, but about consistency in upholding the rule of law," Adnan said while debating the 2027 budget in the Dewan Rakyat.

Under Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution, the attorney-general, who also acts as the public prosecutor, has the discretionary power to institute, conduct or discontinue any criminal proceeding, except proceedings before a shariah court, a native court or a court martial.
Adnan said if Article 145(3) remained in effect, it should be applied in a constitutional manner.

"If the government believes that the power structure of the attorney-general and public prosecutor needs to be amended to strengthen prosecutorial independence and accountability, it should seriously consider constitutional and institutional reforms rather than resort to political interference in specific cases," he added.

Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor) interjected, saying he agreed with Adnan's arguments but that Adnan should address whether the attorney-general should intervene in cases where the courts had made findings supported by solid evidence and called on the accused to enter their defence.
In response, Adnan said the attorney-general previously decided to discontinue a case in which up to 25 witnesses were called, although he did not specify which case.
He said if the attorney-general’s discretionary powers under Article 145(3) needed to be amended, the change should be made in the Dewan Rakyat.

"I also disagree (with the exercise of the attorney-general’s powers in cases) where the court has made a decision. But I have to accept it as the rule of law, a legal process in our country until we make a decision to amend and change Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution," he added.
Adnan was commenting on Zahid's case after RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) called for Zahid to be charged again in the Yayasan Akalbudi corruption case during a debate on the 2027 budget on Oct 12.

Zahid was granted a discharge not amounting to an acquittal in 2023 on 47 charges of corruption in the Yayasan Akalbudi case, which the prosecution said was to allow the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission to conduct further investigations.
The case was classified as requiring no further action in January.
6a2f12484ea80964: JAKARTA: Malaysia is exploring opportunities for collaboration with Netflix to develop the country as a destination for post-production activities in the film and creative industry.

The Malaysian delegation also included Malaysia's Ambassador-designate to Indonesia Datuk Muzafar Shah Mustafa, MyCreative Ventures Group Chief Executive Officer Zainol Haqim Zainol Rashid, National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) Chief Executive Officer Datuk Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib and Bernama Deputy Editor-in-Chief (News Services) Mohd Shukri Ishak.
Fahmi said discussions also covered Netflix's selection process for films and productions, which could help Malaysian films, animation and intellectual property (IP) reach international audiences.

"This was my first discussion with Netflix, focusing on the creative economy, particularly the film and animation sectors. We have significant potential to bring Malaysian IP and creative works to international markets, potentially through a more accessible route than theatrical distribution in foreign countries.
"We want to understand Netflix's mechanisms for selecting films and productions, whether for production in a particular country or for streaming," he said.
He said Netflix had agreed to visit Kuala Lumpur to view Finas' new office, with further discussions on potential cooperation expected.
He added that Finas hoped Netflix would consider holding some of its regional training programmes in Kuala Lumpur or other locations in Malaysia.
Fahmi arrived in Jakarta yesterday after attending Bali Tech Week. He is scheduled to remain in the Indonesian capital until tomorrow to attend the World Conference on Creative Economy (WCCE).

8745831bac22796f: SAN FRANCISCO: OpenAI said on Tuesday that two of its AI agents weakened parts of an internal monitoring system designed to detect misbehavior, the latest case of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend them to.

While the ChatGPT maker said the incidents happened during internal coding tasks and were not deemed its most severe, the disclosure highlights even the systems developers rely on to catch AI misbehaviour are vulnerable to the agents they monitor.
The disclosure also comes amid growing concerns that AI safety efforts are lagging behind the rapid development of increasingly powerful systems.
Researchers have warned that advanced AI agents could become harder to monitor and control as they gain greater autonomy.
Developers, including IPO-bound rivals OpenAI and Anthropic, have revealed in recent months instances of their AI agents accessing external systems without authorisation.

OpenAI said On Tuesday a GPT-6.1 Sol agent working on an internal testing task on Oct 3 suppressed automatic security alerts after deciding an earlier instruction not to send Slack messages also covered safety notifications.
In a separate incident on Oct 6, a GPT-6 Astra agent removed a safety monitor while copying an existing piece of code and later incorrectly claimed it had not done so, OpenAI said.
"In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them," the company said.
OpenAI said it was making it harder for models to disable monitoring, adding that it does not "yet have a satisfying explanation for this behavior."
The San Francisco-based company said it was testing whether its models might have a tendency to avoid being monitored and look for reasons to justify doing so.

30269259aa6946dc: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 21 — Ten former Negeri Sembilan state executive council (exco) members have filed an application in the Federal Court seeking to challenge the state ruler’s decision last month to revoke their appointments.

The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Datuk Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
They named the Negeri Sembilan state secretary and the state government as respondents.
They filed the notice of motion on October 14 this year through law firm Messrs Hafarizam Wan & Aisha Mubarak.

In the notice of motion, they want the Federal Court to determine three questions concerning the effect and interpretation of the provisions of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution, which have arisen in their originating summons filed in the Seremban High Court.
On October 5 this year, they filed the originating summons to challenge the validity of a gazette revoking their appointments as exco members.
In their originating summons, they raised several constitutional questions.

Among the questions is whether Article 38(5), read together with Articles 38(2), 38(3), 38(4), 40(1), 40(1A) and 40(2) of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution, allows the Yang Dipertuan Besar to revoke the appointment of an exco without the Menteri Besar’s advice.

If the answer to that question is negative, whether the revocation of the exco members’ appointments, as gazetted on Sept 24 this year, was done in accordance with the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 and therefore null, void and ineffective.

Another question is whether, under Article 38(5), read together with Article 28(1) of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution, the expression “Ruler” shall mean the Yang Dipertuan Besar alone at his pleasure can revoke the appointment of an exco without the advice of the Menteri Besar. If the answer to the above is in the negative, whether their dismissal is unconstitutional.
On September 20, the Negeri Sembilan palace announced that the Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, had revoked the appointments of the exco members with immediate effect.
The revocation of their appointments was gazetted on Sept 24, with their removal effective Sept 20.

The gazette stated that their appointments were revoked and annulled because they violated their pledge of allegiance to Tuanku Muhriz when they agreed on Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
A case management is scheduled before the Federal Court Deputy Registrar today. — Bernama

628157b38bc08a2e: MUMBAI: Jio Platforms' US$3.2 billion IPO was 85% subscribed within the first hour of public bidding on Wednesday, as investors flocked to India's largest share sale and the first from billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance in two decades.

The Jio Platforms IPO will be a major test of global appetite for new share offerings at a time when investors have sharpened their scrutiny of AI-related companies, which some analysts say could see them pivoting away from the technology.

With backing from Meta, Alphabet's Google and institutional investors, Jio Platforms is home to India's biggest telecom company with more than 500 million subscribers, making it the world's second-largest telecom operator in a single country ​after China Mobile.

Institutional investors have bid for 2.8 times their reserved portion in the IPO. Retail investors, for whom around a third of the issue is reserved, have so far bid for 0.14 times their quota, exchange data showed on Wednesday.

The IPO values Jio Platforms at up to US$108.3 billion, potentially making it one of India's biggest companies by market capitalisation when trading starts on Oct 28, with around a third of the shares on offer reserved for retail investors.

Jio Platforms this week allotted shares worth US$853 million to ‌global ⁠and domestic investors including Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock after the reserved portion for such investors drew bids totalling more than US$25 billion.
Retail investors, employees and shareholders of Reliance will get to participate in the offering that closes on Friday and has a price range set at 1,065 to 1,119 rupees per share.
The IPO is the first from Reliance since 2006 and is bigger than previous major listings such as Hyundai Motor India and National Stock Exchange.
Ambani first promised a listing within five years in 2019, and the plans were also delayed in 2025. A filing for as early as March was pushed back after the Iran war dampened IPO appetite.

Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began in 2016 with a bet that Indians would use the internet far more if it cost almost nothing. It rapidly took market share from rivals such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea by offering cheap data and free voice calls.
Jio Platforms is pitching its IPO during an ongoing Hindu festive season, which is considered auspicious for purchases, but when Indian markets have remained subdued in recent weeks.

Reliance paid its more than 400,000 employees their salaries about 15 days early this month, and the company helped facilitate share account opening services in recent weeks to those interested in applying for the IPO, a person in the industry with direct knowledge of the situation said.
Reliance did not respond to a request for comment.
Jio Platforms earned about US$3.2 billion in profit on US$15.5 billion of revenue in the year to March. Around 90% of those figures were attributable to its telecoms business alone.

56051b5c1a102b05: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated national para-athletics ace Datuk Abdul Latif Romly for displaying exceptional fighting spirit to clinch his fourth consecutive gold medal in the men's T20 long jump at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.

639bc38f21a89fea: SEOUL: South Korean authorities began a new attempt Wednesday to coax a shark-turned-viral sensation back to sea, with falling temperatures in the Busan canal where it is stranded raising concerns for its survival.

The dusky shark – affectionately nicknamed "Bukhangi" by fans – was spotted last month in an artificial waterway in the southeastern port city, with climate activists linking its appearance to climate change.

The three-metre shark, a species typically found in tropical climates, has since amassed a huge following, drawing more than 1.6 million people to the Busan canal for a glimpse in person – bringing an unexpected boon to the local economy.
South Korean authorities twice tried unsuccessfully to steer Bukhangi back to sea – using water jets and then nets – before launching a third attempt Wednesday as the water grows colder.
"The operation began at 10 am this morning, and we are not entirely sure when it's going to end – given our previous attempts were not successful," an oceans ministry official told AFP.
Officials initially opted to wait for the shark to leave on its own, but growing overall concerns for its well-being prompted a third attempt, she added.
In a separate statement, the ministry said the limited water depth in the artificial waterway also prompted authorities to decide to launch their third attempt.
Busan authorities livestreamed the operation as curious onlookers gathered along the canal for another glimpse of the shark.
For Wednesday's operation, authorities fixed nets to floating pontoons, to be moved gradually as the shark heads towards the open sea.
Once it passes, the nets will block its return to the waterway, they said.
The shark has also been celebrated for its unexpected boost to the local economy, with Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo thanking it for generating publicity he said would otherwise have cost "trillions."
But environmental groups say the shark's appearance should be seen as a warning of the climate crisis, rather than a spectacle or economic boost.
They link its arrival to warming seas, saying rising temperatures are pushing warm-water fish northward – and subtropical sharks in pursuit.
c8d2c915234d7d53: LOS ANGELES: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said the Oklahoma City Thunder are "hungry" for more success after exacting a small measure of revenge on the San Antonio Spurs in their NBA season-opener on Tuesday.

3bbc951bc22d3c2b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — A businessman was charged at the Sessions Court here today with four counts of cheating another businessman, who holds the title Datuk Seri, by claiming he could help resolve issues involving frozen bank accounts and a police investigation into more than RM10 million.
Tan Sri Tan Kean Soon, 63, however, pleaded not guilty to all four charges after they were read out before Judge Azrul Darus.

According to the charges, Tan allegedly cheated businessman Datuk Seri Keh Chuan Seng, 55, by deceiving him into believing that he could help resolve the freezing of Keh’s personal and company bank accounts by police, as well as a police investigation into Keh under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLA).

The deception allegedly induced Keh to hand over cash amounting to RM2 million, RM3 million, SGD1.5 million and RM500,000 to Tan through Datuk Seri Chiau Beng Teik, in which Keh would not have handed over the money had he not been deceived.
The offences were allegedly committed at a car park in Kuchai Lama, Dataran Maybank in Bangsar, Pavilion Hotel and Kampung Pandan here between March 23 and 25, 2025.
The charges were brought under Section 420 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Norfauzani Mohd Nordin did not offer bail, citing the non-bailable nature of the offence and the total amount of money involved, which she said was RM10 million.
“If the court allows bail, the prosecution proposes RM2 million. However, he must notify the court and the prosecution of any overseas travel by letter and email,” she said.
Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, representing Tan, requested bail of RM1 million, saying his client needed to travel regularly to Singapore for medical treatment.
“My client is a businessman and has always cooperated fully with the police,” he said.
Bail was set at RM1 million with one surety, and Tan was ordered to inform the court and the prosecution of any overseas travel. Jan 11, 2027 was fixed for mention. — Bernama
d3eb69fcb27d268e: PUTRAJAYA: Ten former Negri Sembilan state executive councillors have turned to the Federal Court to challenge the revocation of their appointments by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir last month.
They are seeking a ruling on whether the Ruler has the constitutional authority to revoke their appointments without the advice of the menteri besar.

The applicants are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umairah Hashim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
In a notice of motion filed on Oct 14, they challenged the revocation of their appointments, which was gazetted on Sept 24 and stated to take effect from Sept 20.

They are asking the Federal Court to determine whether the revocations were carried out in accordance with the state constitution and, if not, whether they should be declared null, void and ineffective.
The Negri Sembilan State Secretary and the state government have been named as the first and second respondents, respectively.

According to court documents sighted by the New Straits Times, the application was filed under Article XXXIV(2) of the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959, which provides for constitutional questions to be referred to the Federal Court.
The application stems from an originating summons filed by the 10 applicants at the Seremban High Court earlier this month over the revocation of their appointments.
At the centre of the dispute is Article XXXVIII(5) of the state constitution, which provides that a member of the State Executive Council holds office at the pleasure of the Ruler.

The applicants want the Federal Court to determine whether the provision allows the Yang di-Pertuan Besar to withdraw his consent to an executive councillor's appointment without first obtaining the advice of the menteri besar.

They are also seeking clarification on whether the phrase "at the Ruler's pleasure" grants unrestricted powers to revoke such appointments, regardless of other constitutional provisions governing the exercise of royal powers.

Another question raised is whether the reference to the "Ruler" under Article XXXVIII(5), when read together with Article XXVIII(1), empowers the Yang di-Pertuan Besar to act independently of the menteri besar's advice.

The applicants are seeking a determination on whether the revocation, published in the Negri Sembilan Government Gazette under N.S. P.U. 18 on Sept 24, would be unconstitutional and invalid if the Ruler was required to act on such advice.
The constitutional questions also involve Articles XXXVIII(2), XXXVIII(3), XXXVIII(4), XL(1), XL(1A) and XL(2) of the state constitution.

The applicants want the Federal Court to determine the constitutional questions before either disposing of the underlying case or returning it to the Seremban High Court for disposal in accordance with its ruling.
They are also seeking an expedited hearing, citing the significance of the constitutional issues and their implications for the positions of state executive councillors.
The applicants said the originating summons remained unresolved and were scheduled for case management at the Seremban High Court today.
The controversy began on Sept 20 when the palace announced that Tuanku Muhriz had revoked the appointments of all 10 state executive councillors with immediate effect.

The palace said the decision followed their actions and statements on Sept 15, which it said were inconsistent with the oath they had taken to remain loyal to the Ruler and the royal institution, uphold the state constitution and recognise the authority of the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang.

Kira-kira 500 peguam berhimpun di Padang Merbok pada 17 Jun 2022 dengan tujuan berarak ke Parlimen untuk menyerahkan memorandum yang menggesa kerajaan mempertahankan kebebasan kehakiman.

Majlis Peguam menganjurkan perarakan itu bagi membantah dakwaan intimidasi terhadap badan kehakiman, khususnya siasatan Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) yang melibatkan seorang hakim yang masih berkhidmat.
New Sin Yew dan Nur Izni Syazwani Ahmad mewakili Majlis Peguam, manakala Peguam Kanan Persekutuan Al-Saifi Hashim dan Peguam Persekutuan Ashraf Abdul Hamid bertindak bagi pihak kerajaan.
b7c19ee8a94e6ea1: PETALING JAYA: The government has banned civil servants from using the popular navigation app Waze, which was developed in Israel.
In a letter dated Oct 20, Chief Secretary Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the decision was made at a National Cybersecurity Committee meeting chaired by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim earlier that day.
"All heads of departments and secretaries-general must ensure that staff are informed of the decision for immediate implementation," the letter said.
It said the National Cyber Security Agency under the National Security Council of the Prime Minister’s Department was the coordinating agency for the directive’s implementation.
Anwar encouraged Malaysians on social media to consider using TuJu, a local navigation app developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority.
He cited concerns over Waze's personal data security and information on users' movements, given that the navigation app is subject to Israeli government laws.
Malaysia joins Iraq, which has announced a complete ban on Waze effective 2027.
Iran also previously blocked and restricted access to Waze due to its links to Israel.

In 2017, Malaysia was reported to have one of the highest numbers of Waze users in Asia, with about six million monthly active users, including around 2.5 million in Kuala Lumpur. Users generated nearly 1.2 million traffic alerts a month.
Google acquired Waze in June 2013 for about US$1.15 billion. The app was founded in Israel in 2008 by three Israeli entrepreneurs.

c324ed6ce6a869c8: OCTOBER 21 — Section 16 of the Societies Act (Revised 2021) reads as follows:

(1) If the Registrar is of the opinion that a dispute has occurred among the members or office-bearers of a registered society as a result of which the Registrar is not satisfied of the identity of the persons who have been properly constituted as office-bearers of the society, the Registrar may serve notice on the society requiring the society, within one month of the service of such notice, to produce to him evidence of the settlement of any such dispute and of the proper appointment of the lawful office-bearers of the society or of the institution of proceedings for the settlement of such dispute.

(2) If any such notice as is provided in subsection (1) is not complied with to the satisfaction of the Registrar within the period of one month or any extension of the period allowed by the Registrar, the Registrar may take steps to cancel the registration of the society under Section 13.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Section 13(1)(c)(ix) provides that the Registrar of Societies (ROS) may cancel the registration of any registered society if the ROS is satisfied that the registered society has failed to comply with the notice served by the ROS under Section 16(1). — Unsplash pic

Section 13(1)(c)(ix) provides that the Registrar of Societies (ROS) may cancel the registration of any registered society if the ROS is satisfied that the registered society has failed to comply with the notice served by the ROS under Section 16(1).
In the case of Pendaftar Pertubuhan v Datuk Justin Jinggut [2013] the Federal Court had occasion to construe Sections 16(1) and 13(1)(c)(ix) of the Act.
Delivering the apex court’s judgment, Federal Court Judge Abdull Hamid Embong said:

“This appeal involves the statutory interpretation of Sections 16 and 13 of the Act. On a literal interpretation of Section 16(1), we are of the view that the ROS … merely needs to act on the documents presented to him to objectively decide if a dispute had arisen. Once he is satisfied, and here we say on a subjective test, that a dispute had in fact occurred, he may straight away form such an opinion. We say that this is his only statutory duty.
“The word ‘opinion’ as found in Section 16(1) entails a subjective evaluation by the ROS. It is defined in the Concise Oxford Dictionary as ‘according to one’s view or belief’.

“[The ROS] forms this opinion based on the documents and information before him …. No detective work is required of the ROS to form this opinion. Otherwise, the office of the ROS would be bogged down to make unnecessary inquiries each time he is faced with information of a dispute having occurred in a political society.

“Under Section 16(1)… [the ROS] merely comes to an opinion of the existence of a dispute. And this he needs to do as quickly as possible. Otherwise, the fate of a society will be left in a limbo, and all its activities suspended.

“We say that the ROS role is one of non-interference in a dispute situation involving a political society …. Once he was satisfied, on a subjective test, that a dispute had in fact occurred, he could straight away form such an opinion.”
The learned Federal Court judge then went on to say:

“In our considered view, for the court to go behind the opinion stated by the ROS … this would be usurping the limited powers of the ROS under Section 16(1). The court would then have to substitute the subjective opinion of the ROS.
“In other words, it would take over the role of the ROS, which we say we cannot do.”
Construing Sections 16(1) and 13(1)(c)(ix), the learned Federal Court judge said:

“It is our considered opinion that Section 16(1) empowers the ROS to direct [the political party] to put its house back in order. In other words, the ROS merely gives [the political party] an ultimatum to settle the dispute or face the peril of cancellation under Section 13(1)(c)(ix).

“The phrase used in subsection (1)(c) is ‘if the ROS is satisfied’. ‘Satisfy’ as defined in the Concise Oxford Dictionary is to ‘be certain in one’s own mind’, meaning that a subjective test is to be applied to the ROS in considering whether there has been compliance with the Section 16(1) notice.
“The notice [which was] sent to the secretary general of [the political party] simply states that the party [is] to take steps to settle the dispute within one month.

“Section 16(2) of the Act states that if any such notice as is provided in subsection (1) is not complied with to the satisfaction of the ROS within the period of one month or any extension thereof allowed by the ROS, the ROS may take steps to cancel the registration of the society under Section 13.
“Now, [having] been satisfied that there has been a non-compliance of his notice, [the ROS] can act under Section 13(1)(c)(ix) of the Act to cancel the registration of [the political party].

“Thus, if no evidence … is forthcoming from [the political party] and if the ROS is satisfied that there has been a failure to comply with the Section 16(1) notice, then he may cancel the registration of [the political party].
It must be minded that the only basis for cancellation of a society’s registration under Section 13(1)(c)(ix) is for non-compliance of a Section 16(1) notice.
It was emphasized by the Federal Court that once the ROS is satisfied with this failure to comply, the ROS may accordingly act to de-register a society.

The decision to de-register a society is merely consequential to the failure of the society to comply. Once the conditions stated in the Section 16(1) notice have not been satisfied, the operation of Section 13(1)(c)(ix) is triggered.
No reasons are required under the law.
No reasons need to be given.
*This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
6a604ed626706964: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Amanat Lebuhraya Rakyat Berhad (ALR) has crossed the RM2 billion threshold in cumulative sukuk principal and profit repayments, positioning the private not-for-profit firm to return four major Klang Valley toll highways to the government by 2033, five years ahead of schedule.

The milestone validates ALR’s enterprise model of using surplus toll collection solely to extinguish acquisition debt without paying dividends to shareholders, clearing the path for the state to take back the Kesas Expressway, Lebuhraya Damansara-Puchong (LITRAK), Western Kuala Lumpur Traffic Dispersal Scheme (SPRINT), and the Stormwater Management and Road Tunnel (SMART).

“On October 13, 2026, ALR made its eight sukuk payment of RM513.8 million comprising RM390 million to Sukuk Principal and RM123.8 million to Sukuk Profit, bringing its cumulative Sukuk Principal and Profit payments to more than RM2.149 billion.

“The Sustainability Sukuk Murabahah Programme carries total sukuk principal and profit obligations of RM7.935 billion,” ALR group chief executive officer Muhammad Nizam Alias told a media briefing at the SMART headquarters here today.
The latest debt servicing payment follows an earlier benchmark in April 2025, when cumulative payments touched RM1.021 billion.
“Surpassing RM2 billion in cumulative sukuk payments represents an important milestone in ALR’s journey.

“It demonstrates our continued financial discipline and commitment to meeting our obligations while remaining focused on the mandate entrusted to us to maintain toll affordability, eliminate the need for government compensation payments and accelerate the return of the highways to the government and the rakyat,” Muhammad Nizam said.
He explained that because ALR distributes no dividends, all net operational income flows directly toward servicing liabilities and sustaining day-to-day asset management.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Amanat Lebuhraya Rakyat Bhd group chief executive officer Muhammad Nizam Alias speaks during a press conference at the SMART Tunnel in Kuala Lumpur on October 21, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif

“The milestone reflects the progress ALR has made since the issuance of the Sustainability Sukuk Murabahah in October 2022 and reinforces the connection between the group’s financial discipline and its long-term public-interest mandate.

“ALR issued RM5.5 billion in nominal value of AAA-rated Senior Sustainable and Responsible Investment Sukuk Murabahah on October 13, 2022 to finance the acquisition of four major urban highway concessionaires — KESAS, LITRAK, SPRINT and SMART.
“The acquisition was undertaken without the use of public funds or a government guarantee,” he said.

Established strictly as a transitional custodial entity, ALR freezes toll charges at existing gazetted levels throughout the tenure rather than imposing contractual hikes that require federal compensation payouts.
“Under its model, toll rates will remain at current levels until the respective concessions end, while surplus revenue is channelled towards the early redemption of debt financing,” he said.
Strong commuter traffic across the four networks has bolstered debt redemption timelines, setting up a potential full settlement well before the paper’s final maturity date in 2038.
“Under the sukuk programme, the longest maturity is 15 years, ending in 2038.
“However, based on our projections, the surplus accumulated each year could be sufficient by 2033 to settle the remaining sukuk obligations in a lump sum.
“The sooner we settle the entire sukuk amount, the sooner we can return the highways to the government.
“The government can then decide what to do with the highways, whether to charge nominal toll rates or make them toll-free.”
Alongside its role as a key bypass artery easing gridlock between Kuala Lumpur and the southern corridor, the dual-purpose SMART Tunnel plays a vital flood mitigation function for the city centre.

Since commencing operations in May 2007, the subterranean tunnel has diverted 266.03 million cubic metres of deluge over 685 flood-activation events, preventing an estimated RM4.94 billion in structural damage and public losses.
“Operating and maintaining critical infrastructure such as the SMART Tunnel required substantial financial resources.
“Nevertheless, it remained committed to its social responsibilities and continued to balance operational expenditure with toll revenue while meeting its sukuk obligations,” Muhammad Nizam said.

ALR maintains that its non-profit holding structure will continue to balance high engineering maintenance standards with steady debt retirement, ensuring motorists face no toll increases until the four concessions are formally returned to Putrajaya.
01c488671c61a914: KUALA LUMPUR: Hadi Awang (PAS-Marang) mengingatkan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim memilih penasihat yang berani menegur kesilapan, bukannya pengampu hanya mementingkan diri sendiri.

Menyentuh belanjawan, Hadi mempersoalkan peningkatan defisit, hutang negara dan cukai, sambil menegaskan keberkesanan belanjawan perlu diukur berdasarkan manfaat kepada rakyat, bukan keuntungan kerajaan, syarikat korporat atau kroni.

8967b6dd4fe3f41e: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 21 — The Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (CVLB) Sabah will take action against the operator of the trailer truck involved in the fatal accident near Sepanggar Port on Sunday.
Chairman Datuk Phoong Jin Zhe said the board will meet on Oct 30 to discuss and finalise appropriate action against the operator.
He stressed that CVLB will not compromise on any negligence or breaches of regulations that could endanger road users.
This includes considering recommendations to suspend or revoke the relevant licence, subject to the findings of the investigation and applicable laws and regulations, he said.
He said CVLB Sabah will also continue to work closely with the Royal Malaysia Police and Road Transport Department (JPJ) to ensure that firm legal action is taken against those responsible.
In the incident on Sunday, a 53-year-old man and his 24-year-old daughter were killed when a container fell onto the car they were travelling in near Sepanggar Port.
Initial investigations found that the trailer had stopped on the left lane to load a container from the roadside onto the vehicle.
The container then fell onto a passing car.
It took firefighters more than three hours to extricate the victims from the wrecked car.
Both victims were pronounced dead at the scene by the paramedics and their bodies were later taken to Queen Elizabeth I Hospital for a post-mortem.

The 49-year-old trailer truck driver was detained by police to assist with investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing the death of another person by driving a motor vehicle on a road recklessly or dangerously. — The Borneo Post
1d28ee6b783c1550: PETALING JAYA: PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang today said that all aspects of Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) administration and management were handled in accordance with its constitution, in response to Bersatu president Muhyiddin Yassin’s claim that PN's deregistration stemmed from its leaders' failure to act constitutionally and in accordance with the law.

f4f83f45ea442393: PARIS, Oct 21 — Announcements over recent months that artificial intelligence models have cracked previously unsolvable problems are shaking to the core top-level mathematicians, who are now asking themselves: where do we come in?

“All the avenues of research I had are now gone; we’re facing a new day,” Hugo Duminil-Copin, winner of the 2022 Fields Medal, one of the highest honours in mathematics, recently told his colleagues at the French Mathematical Society.
Since April, AI firms have regularly been publishing solutions to previously unsolved mathematical problems as they seek to demonstrate the power of their latest models.
Last week, OpenAI released solutions to 719 previously unsolved problems.
The advances are forcing those in the field to wonder whether this spells the end of mathematical research.
Thinking tool

While acknowledging the emotional shock caused by the recent publications, Stephane Mallat, 2025 Gold Medal recipient from France’s national scientific research centre (CNRS), told AFP there will always be a need for mathematicians.
“Mathematics goes far beyond calculation: it’s a way of thinking clearly,” Mallat said.
“Beyond all the problems we face with AI, maths will remain absolutely central because it’s a tool that allows us humans to think clearly and understand things,” he told AFP.
An initial sign of pushback from the field has come from the Simons Foundation.
This major American patron of mathematics announced last week a US$15-million (RM61.2-million) programme co-funded by OpenAI and Anthropic to support mathematicians in dealing with AI.
It will fund workshops to assess the results produced by AI and establish standards for its use.
Mallat also noted mathematicians are needed for teaching, although the rapid advancement of AI will impact this area too.

“You have a lot of young people who aren’t very keen on doing maths, and when you see an impact like this, they might say: ‘Oh well, even researchers are going to be replaced by AI, so why should I bother?’” said Mallat.
“That question needs to be addressed, because it’s completely false that we no longer need mathematicians.”
Tractors and Columbo
For Francois Charles, mathematician and department head at the Ecole Normale Superieure in Paris, two separate issues are playing out.

“We have legitimate concerns about how the community is organised, because AI is bringing a number of changes in how people enter the profession or at the doctoral level. But on the purely scientific side, I’m not at all pessimistic,” he said.
“A certain number of obstacles may be overcome. As scientists, we need to be more ambitious.”
Mallat, who has recently published a book on maths and AI, makes a distinction between what is happening and the mechanisation of agriculture when tractors came on the scene.

“It was also a human tragedy for some who had to abandon the countryside, move to the cities, find jobs, retrain. Now, mathematicians are not in that situation. When you know how to do maths, you can do an enormous number of things,” he argued.
Meanwhile, in the pages of French daily Le Figaro, 2010 Fields Medallist Cedric Villani, a strong critic of AI, took inspiration from the TV detective Columbo.
“In mathematics, the conclusion is less important than the path to get there.” — AFP
1247f8c9321774bb: PETALING JAYA: Seorang pemimpin Pemuda Bersatu hari ini mendakwa PAS cuba melemahkan partinya dan menjadikan Wawasan pimpinan Hamzah Zainudin sebagai pengganti Bersatu dalam Perikatan Nasional (PN).
Ketua Penerangan Pemuda Bersatu, Harris Idaham Rashid, mendakwa pemimpin PAS mendesak supaya Bersatu diketepikan dan Wawasan diberi kedudukan lebih tinggi dalam gabungan itu.
“Namun, rancangan itu gagal susulan pembatalan pendaftaran PN oleh Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia (JPPM),” katanya dalam satu kenyataan.

Harris turut mempertahankan aduan Bersatu kepada JPPM dengan menegaskan bahawa parti itu mematuhi peraturan selepas wakilnya dinafikan hak untuk hadir, bersuara dan mengundi dalam mesyuarat Majlis Tertinggi PN pada 16 Julai.

Beliau berkata Bersatu mengemukakan lapan alasan berhubung dakwaan pelanggaran perlembagaan PN, termasuk penafian hak mengundi wakilnya, ketiadaan notis mesyuarat yang sah, korum yang didakwa tidak mencukupi serta pelantikan ke jawatan penting tanpa persetujuan sebulat suara parti komponen.

Harris turut menuduh kepimpinan PN mengubah struktur organisasi gabungan itu tanpa kelulusan rasmi Majlis Tertingginya, selain mengetepikan sebuah parti komponen utama dalam keputusan berkaitan dasar dan hala tuju.
Harris menolak dakwaan Ketua Penerangan Wawasan Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal bahawa Bersatu mengkhianati PN dengan mengemukakan aduan itu.

Wan Fayhsal, bekas anggota Majlis Pimpinan Tertinggi Bersatu, menuduh parti itu merancang pembatalan pendaftaran PN selepas kehilangan jawatan kepimpinan dalam gabungan berkenaan, kononnya bagi membuka jalan kepada kerjasama dengan Pakatan Harapan (PH).
Bagaimanapun, Harris menegaskan aduan Bersatu itu berasas dengan alasan hak parti berkenaan dinafikan dalam mesyuarat pada 16 Julai.
Beliau turut membayangkan tuduhan Wan Fayhsal itu berkait dengan kelangsungan politik Wawasan.
“Wawasan tidak mempunyai banyak pengaruh politik tanpa PN sebagai platformnya. Percubaan parti itu menumpang populariti gabungan berkenaan demi kelangsungan politiknya sendiri akhirnya memakan diri.”
2e6e1a56586a16ee: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Bar and four former Bar Council office-bearers were awarded a total of RM59,449 in damages after the Court of Appeal found that police breached their constitutional rights by imposing unlawful restrictions on a 2022 march for judicial independence.

In partly allowing the Bar’s appeal, a three-member bench chaired by Justice Choo Kah Sing awarded RM19,449 in special damages to the Bar, and RM10,000 each to former office-bearers Karen Cheah, Ezri Abdul Wahab, B Anand Raj and Murshidah Mustafa.
Justices Faizah Jamaludin and Lim Hock Leng were also on the panel.
Delivering the judgment, Choo said Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) consent was not required for the assembly at Padang Merbok, contrary to the High Court’s finding.
The court also ruled that the Bar's notification to the police under Section 9 of the Peaceful Assembly Act 2012 was valid.
Choo said a letter from the Dang Wangi police chief imposing conditions on the march was issued outside the prescribed period.

The Bar notified police on June 3 but received the response only on June 16, less than 24 hours before the assembly, he said. Under Section 14 of the Act, police must respond with any conditions within three days.
However, the court upheld the High Court's dismissal of the false imprisonment claim, finding that the participants were not totally deprived of their liberty.
"While participants were prohibited from marching to Parliament House, they were not physically restrained from leaving the area," Choo said.

The court also upheld the finding that the police were not liable for misfeasance in public office, but dismissed the claim for misconduct in public office, saying it failed to meet the high subjective threshold required.
Despite finding constitutional violations, the bench did not award general damages, including aggravated or punitive damages.
Instead, it ordered interest of 5% a year from the date of the High Court judgment until full settlement, with no order as to costs.
About 500 lawyers gathered at Padang Merbok on June 17, 2022, intending to march to Parliament to submit a memorandum urging the government to uphold judicial independence.
The Bar organised the march to protest the alleged intimidation of the judiciary, particularly an investigation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission involving a sitting judge.
New Sin Yew and Nur Izni Syazwani Ahmad represented the Bar while senior federal counsel Al-Saifi Hashim and federal counsel Ashraf Abdul Hamid acted for the government.
e3a1feafc2620eef: PETALING JAYA: Anggota perkhidmatan awam dilarang menggunakan aplikasi navigasi Waze berkuat kuasa serta merta susulan keputusan Jawatankuasa Keselamatan Siber Negara (JKSN).

Arahan itu terkandung dalam surat Ketua Setiausaha Negara Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar bertarikh 20 Okt, yang ditujukan kepada ketua setiausaha kementerian, ketua jabatan persekutuan, pengurusan badan berkanun persekutuan, setiausaha kerajaan negeri dan ketua pengurusan pihak berkuasa tempatan.
Menurut surat itu, keputusan melarang penggunaan Waze, yang disifatkan sebagai aplikasi navigasi 'berpangkalan di negara Israel', dibuat pada mesyuarat JKSN, semalam.
Mesyuarat berkenaan dipengerusikan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.

Shamsul Azri mengarahkan semua ketua setiausaha kementerian dan ketua jabatan memastikan keputusan itu dimaklumkan kepada pegawai di bawah seliaan kementerian, agensi dan jabatan masing-masing untuk dilaksanakan serta-merta.
Mereka juga diminta memastikan arahan itu dipatuhi sepenuhnya di semua peringkat kementerian, jabatan dan agensi.

114434d524dea998: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The High Court has granted an interim stay on the Malaysian Bar’s judicial review challenging the Attorney General’s decision to halt corruption proceedings against Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The decision freezes the challenge until the Federal Court disposes of the government’s appeal.
Justice Azizan Arshad granted the stay order in chambers today following an application by the Attorney General (AG), according to Zahid’s lawyer Guok Ngek Seong, FMT reported.

The freeze halts High Court proceedings after the Federal Court recently granted both the AG and the deputy prime minister leave to challenge an earlier Court of Appeal verdict that had permitted the Malaysian Bar to pursue its judicial review.
“The Federal Court has yet to fix a hearing date for the appeal as the notice of appeal was only filed on Oct 19,” Guok said.
Federal counsel Safiyyah Omar and Imtiyaz Wizni Aufa Othman appeared for the AG, while counsel S Abhilaash represented the Malaysian Bar.

Earlier this month, the apex court ruled that the AG and Zahid satisfied the statutory threshold under Section 96 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964, clearing the way for full substantive arguments on whether prosecutorial discretion under Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution is amenable to judicial review in such circumstances.
That decision paused the momentum generated by the Court of Appeal on May 7, when a three-judge panel unanimously overturned the High Court’s initial refusal to grant leave to the Bar.

The appellate court had reasoned that the Bar’s legal challenge was aimed directly at the “executive root”, namely the AG’s discretionary decision to discontinue the trial, rather than the criminal court’s subsequent judicial order granting Zahid a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA).

Zahid was granted a DNAA by the Kuala Lumpur High Court in September 2023 across all 47 criminal breach of trust, corruption, and money laundering charges involving millions of ringgit from charitable foundation Yayasan Akalbudi, after the prosecution applied to discontinue the case despite having established a prima facie case.

c0d880d40559ebd1: PARIS, Oct 21 — Global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions are falling far short of the Paris climate goals and put the world on course for 2.6°C warming this century, the UN warned today.

The report by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) lays bare the chasm between rhetoric and action when it comes to tackling global warming, and the challenge before political leaders at November’s COP31 climate summit.
Even if countries deliver their latest climate pledges in full, global temperatures could still rise 2.6°C above pre-industrial levels by 2100, said the annual Emissions Gap Report.

That would blow past the historic goal agreed in Paris: keeping warming well below 2°C while striving for a safer 1.5°C. Any chance of keeping to 1.5°C had been “lost” due to decades of insufficient climate action, the report said.
“The world can no longer avoid overshooting the 1.5-degree limit, and the consequences are already devastating,” said UN chief Antonio Guterres in a statement to launch the closely-watched report.
“Deadly floods, brutal heatwaves, raging wildfires, lost lives, crippled economies, deepening inequalities, and those least responsible are suffering first and worst.”
Overall, global greenhouse gas emissions in 2025 were broadly on a par with record levels in 2024, with the difference between the two years too small to call, the report said.
Carbon emissions just from burning coal, oil and gas — the main driver of climate change — rose slightly in 2025 compared to the previous year.

Guterres said deep and immediate cuts were needed to protect humanity from worsening impacts but instead “emissions remain at record levels. And national climate plans and current policies fall dangerously short”.
Sticking just with current policies would see warming hit 2.8°C, the report said.
No country immune

Scientists warn that every additional fraction of a degree above 1.5°C increases extreme weather events and the likelihood of irreversible changes to the planet, from dying coral reefs to melting permafrost.
The world has already warmed roughly 1.4°C relative to pre-industrial times and crossing 1.5°C is expected in a matter of years.
The G20 accounts for three-quarters of global emissions but Guterres said “all countries, especially the big emitters, must do more” to stop heating the planet.

This latest UNEP warming outlook is worse than last year’s due to the formal withdrawal of the United States from the Paris accord and upward revisions of historical emissions, said report co-author Anne Olhoff.
Emissions growth slowed down among the G20 but the US was a “major exception”, it added.
Among the world’s top-six emitters, preliminary data for 2025 showed emissions increases in the US, Indonesia and China and decreases in India, Russia and the European Union.
But in terms of magnitude, the US increase of 133 megatons of CO2 equivalent “far exceeded” that of any other country, driven by higher electricity demand and a rebound of coal power generation.
The next-largest increase was recorded in Turkey, which is hosting the UN climate summit in Antalya from November 9-20.
The US is the world’s second-largest polluter, behind China. US President Donald Trump has called climate change a hoax and rolled back clean energy policies while boosting fossil fuel production.
UNEP executive secretary Inger Andersen told reporters that no country was shielded from climate change and impacts were being felt “on every nation on the planet, including the US”.
‘Historic failure’
The report details a scenario with a 50 per cent chance of bringing global warming back down to 1.5°C by 2100.
To get there, warming must peak around 1.8°C by 2050 and vast amounts of carbon dioxide would have to be removed from the atmosphere to bring temperatures down further.
But this scenario assumes immediate emissions cuts of 6 per cent per year, every year, until 2035 — nowhere near current projections.
“The main takeaway is simple — governments need to get on with enacting policies that cut fossil fuel use as soon as possible,” said Bill Hare, CEO of global policy institute Climate Analytics.
Some climate-vulnerable developing nations have accused bigger emitters of abandoning the Paris goals and a showdown over the 1.5°C target is expected at COP31.

“This is a historic failure of political leadership. The science has been clear for decades, but governments have chosen delay over action. The consequences will be measured in lives lost, not just degrees of warming,” said Mohamed Adow, director of Kenya-based think tank Power Shift Africa.
Guterres agreed there was a climate “leadership gap” but said overshooting 1.5°C “is not surrender”. — AFP

3daeecc8e8095869: JAKARTA: Malaysia is exploring opportunities for collaboration with Netflix to develop the country as a destination for post-production training in the film and creative industry.

"This was my first discussion with Netflix, focusing on the creative economy, particularly the film and animation sectors.

75d984f22bf8022b: Google has fixed the flaws in the Chromium browser engine that saw it poll DNS root servers, but ISPs who seem to have odd views about resilience now emerged as a new source of probably-well-meaning overconsumption of internet resources.

ICANN’s office of the Chief Technology Officer delivered that view on Monday during the governance org’s annual conference in Bali, Indonesia, in a session that shared recent data from its Identifier Technology Health Indicators (ITHI) research program which monitors the security, stability and resilience of the domain name system.

ICANN principal technologist Maud Durand opened with a discussion of “Chromiods” the odd flaw in Chrome that meant well-meaning efforts to avoid a form of DNS hijacking caused the browser to generate about half of all DNS root server traffic during the year 2020.
Given Chrome’s enormous prevalence, that traffic was unwelcome.

ICANN, plus other internetworking and governance stakeholders, told Google to sort it out. Durand said the Chocolate Factory gradually did. ICANN has kept measuring the impact Chrome makes and Durand shared the graph below which shows the browser’s share of DNS root server traffic falling from 45 percent to one percent today.
Or as Durand described it, “in the noise.”
ICANN has now detected a new source of odd DNS traffic: ISPs that use multiple DNS servers for every one of their customers’ requests.

“Every single DNS query is sent three times: to Google, to Cloudflare, and to another DNS resolver,” Durand said, labelling this practice a “belt and suspenders” approach because a single resolver usually suffices to keep services up.
It’s good practice to specify primary and secondary DNS resolvers, in case one doesn’t work. But DNS resolvers are already very resilient, and making multiple requests is unusual.

The ISPs ICANN has spotted send DNS requests over IPv4 and IPv6, and for non-cached requests repeat them within 100 milliseconds for about half of queries. A further 30 percent repeat within thirty seconds.

“It is hard to know if it is a bug or a specific behaviour,” Durand said, before advancing a personal theory that the ISPs who use this odd resilience technique can’t hire skilled internetworking engineers and therefore created a kind of brute-force resilience routine. The organization is researching the cause.

807cd6cdd4d4152d: From P Sundramoorthy

The high-profile investigation into the MBI International Group investment scheme raises a fundamental question about Malaysia’s response to major financial crime: what happens after arrests, raids, and the seizure or freezing of billions of ringgit in assets?
Under Op Northern Star, police announced the arrests of individuals suspected of facilitating the movement or laundering of funds linked to the alleged investment fraud.
By May 2025, authorities reported that 17 people were detained and assets worth approximately RM3.81 billion had been seized or frozen.
Subsequent reporting in January 2026 indicated that 23 people were arrested, with authorities pursuing the forfeiture of hundreds of properties and funds held in bank accounts.

These are significant developments. However, the public deserves clarity about whether investigations are progressing towards lawful outcomes and whether affected investors can realistically expect to recover their losses.
The MBI case should not be judged solely by the number of arrests or the value of assets seized. The real test is what follows.

Complex financial crime investigations require investigators to trace funds, establish individual responsibilities, examine corporate transactions and determine whether assets represent proceeds of unlawful activities.
The reported international dimension of the MBI case adds further challenges, including obtaining foreign evidence and coordinating with overseas enforcement agencies.

An arrest does not establish guilt, and a frozen asset does not automatically represent criminal proceeds. Similarly, release from remand does not necessarily mean a suspect has been cleared or that an investigation has ended.
However, these distinctions should not become a reason for prolonged public uncertainty.
Transparency without compromising investigations

When those previously detained in high-profile investigations return to their daily activities or retain prominent business and social positions, questions inevitably arise. Some may assume allegations have been dismissed, while others may suspect preferential treatment for influential individuals.

Neither conclusion should be drawn merely from a person's release or continued public presence. The presumption of innocence must be respected, and allegations must be established through proper legal proceedings.
The police should provide periodic updates while the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission should clarify the status of any related investigation within its jurisdiction.
Where legally permissible, updates should explain whether investigation papers have been referred to prosecutors and whether charges or asset forfeiture proceedings have commenced.

Where investigations have concluded or decisions have been made not to pursue particular individuals, appropriate clarification should be provided, subject to legal restrictions and the rights of those concerned.
Victims must not be forgotten

Perhaps the most important consideration is the position of investors who lost money through the MBI scheme. Announcements of billions of ringgit in seized or frozen assets may create expectations that investors will eventually recover their losses.
However, the value of seized assets does not necessarily represent the amount available for distribution to victims.
Assets may be subject to competing claims, ownership disputes and forfeiture proceedings. Their eventual recovery and distribution depend on applicable law and the outcomes of legal proceedings.
Authorities should communicate realistic expectations about asset recovery and explain, within legal limits, what mechanisms are available to address victims' claims.
Op Metal a broader lesson

The importance of following investigations through to their outcomes is also illustrated by Op Metal, a separate MACC operation launched in July 2025 targeting an alleged scrap metal and electronic waste smuggling syndicate.

Authorities seized assets worth over RM183 million and froze company and individual bank accounts containing approximately RM51 million. The suspected activities were estimated to have caused the government more than RM950 million in lost export tax revenue over six years.
Op Metal is unrelated to the MBI investment scheme investigation. However, it reinforces a broader lesson: seizures and enforcement announcements are only part of the process.

The MBI case warrants particular attention because of the financial losses suffered by investors and the importance of maintaining confidence in Malaysia's handling of major investment-related fraud allegations.
It presents an opportunity for Malaysian authorities to demonstrate that complex, cross-border financial crime can be confronted with determination, professionalism and transparency.
Ultimately, the public does not expect investigators to reveal everything, but it does expect them to explain what can responsibly be disclosed, demonstrate progress and communicate lawful outcomes.
Justice must extend beyond the headlines.
P Sundramoorthy is a criminologist at the Centre for Policy Research at Universiti Sains Malaysia and an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.

7eac5dc4d24bb6eb: Malaysia's automotive industry has become an interesting battleground between Japan and China, two of the world's great carmaking powers. And the contest is being played out through our national carmakers, Proton and Perodua.
Proton has the backing of Zhejiang Geely, one of China's most technologically advanced automotive groups while Perodua has the support of Daihatsu and, behind it, the industrial might of Toyota.
Both partnerships have been successful, but the arrival of electric vehicles (EV) has changed the rules of the game.

China has taken a commanding lead in EV technology, battery production and manufacturing costs. Japan, despite its dominance of the global automotive industry for decades, has been more cautious about committing itself to battery electric vehicles beyond hybrids.
That puts Perodua in a particularly interesting position.

An important insight into Japan's intentions came in May when its ambassador to Malaysia, Noriyuki Shikata, described Perodua as one of the best examples of a successful Japanese-Malaysian joint venture. More significantly, he disclosed that Japan's economy, trade and industry ministry had decided to extend financial support for a new Perodua-led project.
Shikata also observed that Perodua was entering a new stage of innovation, developing solutions in Malaysia that Japan itself was interested in learning about.

Now, that is an interesting statement coming from the representative of one of the world's most sophisticated automotive nations. For more than three decades in the auto industry, we have regarded the Japanese as the teachers and Malaysians as the students.
Could the relationship now be evolving into something more equal?
From petrol to electric
Consider what Perodua has achieved.

Starting with the modest Kancil in 1994, it has grown into Malaysia's largest carmaker, commanding roughly 40% of our domestic market. Its success was built on affordable, reliable petrol-engine cars, efficient manufacturing and a formidable local supplier network.
The question is whether Perodua can translate these strengths into the electric age.

Its first home-grown EV, the QV-E, represents a bold but expensive undertaking. Unlike Proton, which can draw upon Geely's existing EV platforms and economies of scale, Perodua has invested heavily in developing its own product.
The difference is fundamental. Proton benefits from China's enormous EV ecosystem. Perodua is attempting to develop Malaysian engineering capabilities while building a new supply chain.
Market reception

The QV-E encountered a difficult market reception, with pricing and battery leasing arrangements initially raising questions among buyers. Subsequent price reductions have made it more competitive, but they also illustrate the formidable economics of EV manufacturing.
This is where government policy becomes important. Should Malaysia provide targeted financial assistance to Perodua to develop its EV capabilities?

I believe there is a strong case for doing so, provided the assistance is directed towards research, engineering, local components and technology development rather than simply subsidising car prices as China did for 5 years

There is an even stronger argument if Japan is prepared to participate. Toyota and Daihatsu possess enormous experience in manufacturing efficiency, quality control and supplier development. Combining these strengths with Perodua's local engineering ambitions could create something genuinely valuable.
It would also give Japan an opportunity to develop affordable EV technologies for Asean markets, where price sensitivity remains a major consideration.
Supply chains

We should not overlook that China already enjoys significant advantages in battery technology and scale. Perodua's QV-E itself uses batteries from China's CATL, among the world's biggest maker of EV batteries.
The modern automotive industry depends on international supply chains.
The objective should not be to manufacture every component in Malaysia. It should be to develop technologies and industrial capabilities in which Malaysians can become genuinely competitive.

Nor should this become another exercise in protecting a national carmaker from competition. The government must insist on measurable results, greater localisation, export potential and meaningful Malaysian intellectual property.
Green technology

The transition towards EVs should not be measured solely by the number of electric vehicles sold. The environmental impact of automotive manufacturing, energy consumption, battery production, material sourcing and recycling must also be considered.
Government R&D assistance should therefore include the development and adoption of green technologies and cleaner manufacturing processes throughout Malaysia's automotive industry.
This could include energy-efficient production systems, AI-based energy optimisation, battery recycling, resource efficiency and technologies that reduce industrial emissions.
Such initiatives would not only support environmental sustainability but also improve the competitiveness of Malaysian automotive suppliers in international markets.
Measurable benefits

A proper mechanism should be established to assess the actual national benefits generated by government R&D assistance. Malaysia's New Incentive Framework, introduced in 2026, already moves towards linking investment incentives with measurable economic outcomes.

Rather than creating overlapping subsidy schemes, the government should examine how existing mechanisms can be strengthened and better coordinated to support automotive AI, strategic R&D and green industrial development.
The Japanese ambassador's remarks suggest that Japan sees something worth supporting in Perodua. Malaysia should recognise the opportunity.
Rather than viewing Proton and Perodua simply as two national carmakers competing for domestic sales, perhaps we should see them as two different pathways into the future of automotive manufacturing.
One draws upon China's extraordinary scale and speed. The other could build upon Japan's engineering discipline and Malaysia's own industrial experience.
If both succeed, Malaysia will be the winner. And the one which exports the most is the champion.

5a277e650d119fa6: Tragically simple private keys used by a certification authority based in India have been compromised, meaning the 60-million-plus certs it has issued can’t be trusted and necessitating a massive clean-up job.
The CA of concern in this case is called eMudhra, which boasts of having issued over 60 million digital certificates to help usher in a world of digital trust.
The company has instead panicked the world.
News of the company’s errors appeared on Tuesday in a post by Dennis Jackson, a member of Mozilla’s cryptography engineering team.

“On Saturday, October 17, at 20:06 UTC, Mozilla received a report from a community member that private keys associated with eight eMudhra intermediate certificates had been compromised,” he wrote. “These keys could allow attackers to issue fraudulent HTTPS certificates for websites they do not control.”
Or as Cloudflare put it, “an attacker can create a forged certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate servers to intercept or modify traffic.”

Jackson has since elaborated on the incident and the response, which has thankfully seen Mozilla, Chrome, and Apple remediate the issue so their browsers won’t rely on the certificates – at least after users install an update. He also reports that eMudhra has revoked the certs, and lists many FOSS projects that have issued updates that mean they won’t recognize certs from eMudhra.

That’s welcome, but sadly certs signed with these private keys are still out there and many services rely on them. Browser makers are set up to detect and reject bad certs. Others who relied on them may not be, and will likely need to dig into their environments to see if they rely on certs signed by eMudhra. Developer Geoffrey Huntley has offered some advice on automating that process.
At the time of writing, eMudhra has not responded to The Register’s inquiries about the incident and its security practices.
The latter question is of great interest because security researcher Scott Helme analyzed eMudhra’s certs and found one the private keys it used “is the number 4.”

“Not a number that starts with 4, or the number 4 followed by a few hundred random digits, just, 4... Another one is 56, and another is 115. I know, because I recovered all of them from their public certificates on my laptop just now, and it took less than a second,” Helme wrote.
Other researchers have found private keys including the numbers 66, 155, 156, 230 and 237.
Those are vastly inadequate keys, because they’re easy to guess, making all certs issued by eMudhra susceptible to brute force attacks.
As Helme put it: “A P-384 private key should be a random 384-bit number, which gives you 2³⁸⁴ possibilities (or roughly 10¹¹⁵), so nobody is ever going to search that.”
This is a developing story and The Register will update it as more information becomes available. ®

An October 7, 2026 Discord message from user Torq_boi, said to be Harald Schäfer, Comma.ai’s CTO, implies NovaSpark was distilled from Comma.ai's Rebellious Hope model.

"The claim that NovaSpark is Rebellious Hope with a short fine-tune and an unchanged policy does not survive scrutiny, and we’re not sure how Comma came to that conclusion, especially considering that they do not possess NovaSpark’s model weights or ONNX," the biz said.
In the log data IQ.Lvbs published to support its claims, the company flags the username haraschax as one of those associated with Comma.ai IP addresses. Schäfer uses that username on GitHub.
Comma.ai and Schäfer did not respond to requests for comment sent to several different addresses. The Discord user Torq_boi in the Comma.ai channel did not respond to a DM seeking comment.
